title: Invertible modules on arbitrary affine-space opens over a field are trivial
statement: Let $F$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $n\geq0$, and let $V$ be any open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion] of $\mathbf A^n_F=\operatorname{Spec}(F[t_1,\ldots,t_n])$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Every invertible $\mathcal O_V$-module $L$ [def-sc-invertible-module] admits an $\mathcal O_V$-linear isomorphism $L\simeq\mathcal O_V$. The open $V$ need not be affine or nonempty, and no algebraic-closure hypothesis on $F$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0BDA, lemma-open-subscheme-UFD, final sentence (any open subscheme of affine n-space over a field).

proof.text: Put $A=F[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$ and $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$. Every ideal of $F$ is either zero or generated by $1$: a nonzero member $a$ gives $1=a^{-1}a$. Thus $F$ is Noetherian by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. The identity presentation $A=F[t_1,\ldots,t_n]/(0)$ meets [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], so $A$ is Noetherian. The single affine open $X$ is therefore a Noetherian affine cover, making $X$ locally Noetherian by [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Moreover, [lem-sfb-polynomial-field-ufd] makes $A$ a UFD.

source.place: Tags 00FN, lemma-Noetherian-permanence, and 0BC1, lemma-polynomial-ring-UFD; the Noetherian branch of Divisors Tag 0BDA.

proof.text: For every $x\in X$, clause (c) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], with affine open $X$ itself and $\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)=A$, identifies $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ with $A_{\mathfrak p_x}$. Since $A$ is a UFD, [lem-sfb-ufd-prime-localizations] makes this localization a UFD. In particular every local ring at a point of $X\setminus V$ is a UFD.

source.place: Tag 0BDA, lemma-open-subscheme-UFD, Noetherian case; localization input used in Tag 0BD8, lemma-closure-effective-cartier-divisor. Schemes Tag 01HV, lemma-spec-sheaves, (6).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-invertible-extension-factorial-complement] with $Z=X$, $U=V$, and $M=L$. Its locally Noetherian hypothesis is step 1 and its factorial-complement hypothesis is step 2. It gives an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module $\widetilde L$ and an isomorphism $a:\widetilde L|_V\xrightarrow{\sim}L$. No affineness, density, or nonemptiness of $V$ is required by that statement.

source.place: Tag 0BDA, lemma-open-subscheme-UFD, Noetherian-case reduction by Tag 0BD9, lemma-extend-invertible-module.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-affine-space-invertible-trivial], applied to $F$, $n$, and $\widetilde L$, choose $b:\widetilde L\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal O_X$. Restrict $b$ and its inverse to $V$; they remain inverse because restriction preserves identities and composition. By the definition of an open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion], $\mathcal O_X|_V=\mathcal O_V$. Hence $b|_V\circ a^{-1}:L\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal O_V$ is the required linear isomorphism. This also covers $V=\varnothing$; for $n=0$ the same argument applies to $A=F$.

source.place: Tag 0BDA, lemma-open-subscheme-UFD, Noetherian branch: extend to Spec(A), trivialize there, and restrict.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0BDA, lemma-open-subscheme-UFD, the Noetherian-case proof, using Tag 0BD9 and the already split whole-affine-space case.
